text:
ROXANE:
  On nothing! . . . I shall tell him: Go! Set forth with the reins loose!
  Improvise. Speak of love. Be splendid!

CYRANO (smiling):
  Good.

ROXANE:
  Hush! . . .

CYRANO:
  Hush! . . .

ROXANE:
  Not a word! . . .
  (She goes inside and closes the door again.)

CYRANO (saluting her once the door is closed):
  With thanks to you.
  (The door opens again and Roxane puts her head out.)

ROXANE:
  He might prepare himself! . . .

CYRANO:
  Good Lord, no! . . .

BOTH TOGETHER:
  Hush! . . .
  (The door closes.)

CYRANO (calling):
  Christian!



Scene 3.IV.

Cyrano, Christian.


CYRANO:
  I know everything that is needed. Ready thy memory.
  Here is the chance to cover oneself with glory.
  Let us waste no time. Do not look so sullen.
  Quickly, let us go to thy home; I shall teach thee. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  No!

CYRANO:
  What?

CHRISTIAN:
  No! I am waiting for Roxane here.

CYRANO:
  What fit of madness
  Has seized thee? Come quickly and learn. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  No, I tell thee!
  I am weary of borrowing my letters, my speeches,
  And of playing this role, and of always trembling! . . .
  It was all very well at first! But I feel that she loves me!
  Thank thee. I am no longer afraid. I shall speak for myself.

CYRANO:
  Indeed!

CHRISTIAN:
  And who tells thee that I would not know how? . . .
  I am not so stupid, after all! Thou shalt see!
  But, my dear fellow, thy lessons have been of use to me.
  I shall know how to speak on my own! And, by all the devils,
  I shall always know how to take her in my arms! . . .
  (Noticing Roxane, who is coming out of Clomire’s house again):
  —There she is! Cyrano, no, do not leave me!

CYRANO (saluting him):
  Speak by yourself, sir.
  (He disappears behind the garden wall.)



Scene 3.V.

Christian, Roxane, several male and female précieuses, and the duenna,
for a moment.


ROXANE (emerging from Clomire’s house with a company from whom she
  is taking leave; curtsies and bows):
  Barthénoïde!—Alcandre!—Grémione! . . .

THE DUENNA (despairingly):
  We missed the discourse on Tenderness!
  (She goes into Roxane’s house.)

ROXANE (still taking her leave):
  Urimédonte! . . . Farewell! . . .
  (They all bow to Roxane, bow again to one another, part, and
  move away along different streets. Roxane sees Christian):
  It is you! . . .
  (She goes to him):
  Evening is falling.
  Wait. They are far away. The air is mild. Not a passerby.
  Let us sit down. Speak. I am listening.

CHRISTIAN (sits beside her on the bench. A silence):
  I love you.

ROXANE (closing her eyes):
  Yes, speak to me of love.

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee.

ROXANE:
  That is the theme.
  Embroider upon it, embroider.

CHRISTIAN:
  I. . . you. . .

ROXANE:
  Embroider!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee so much.

ROXANE:
  No doubt! And then?

CHRISTIAN:
  And then. . . I should be so happy
  If you loved me!—Tell me, Roxane, that thou lovest me!

ROXANE (pouting):
  You offer me gruel when I was hoping for cream!
  Tell me a little how you love me? . . .

CHRISTIAN:
  Why. . . greatly.

ROXANE:
  Oh! . . . Lead your feelings out of their labyrinth!

CHRISTIAN (having moved closer and devouring the fair nape of her neck with his eyes):
  Thy neck!
  I should like to kiss it! . . .

ROXANE:
  Christian!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee!

ROXANE (about to rise):
  Again!

CHRISTIAN (quickly, restraining her):
  No! I do not love thee!

ROXANE (sitting down again):
  That is fortunate!

CHRISTIAN:
  I adore thee!

ROXANE (rising and moving away):
  Oh!

CHRISTIAN:
  Yes. . . I am becoming a fool!

ROXANE (dryly):
  And that displeases me!
  As it would displease me if you became ugly.

CHRISTIAN:
  But. . .

ROXANE:
  Go and gather up your fleeing eloquence!

CHRISTIAN:
  I. . .

ROXANE:
  You love me, I know. Farewell.
  (She goes toward the house.)

CHRISTIAN:
  Not yet!
  I shall tell you. . .

ROXANE (pushing open the door to go inside):
  That you adore me. . . yes, I know.
  No! No! Go away!

CHRISTIAN:
  But I. . .
  (She shuts the door in his face.)

CYRANO (who came back in a moment ago without being seen):
  It is a success.



Scene 3.VI.

Christian, Cyrano, the pages, for a moment.


CHRISTIAN:
  Help!

CYRANO:
  No, sir.

CHRISTIAN:
  I shall die if I do not regain
  Her favor this very instant. . .

CYRANO:
  And how the devil can I
  Make you learn this very instant? . . .

CHRISTIAN (seizing his arm):
  Oh! There, look, see!
  (The balcony window has lit up.)

CYRANO (moved):
  Her window!

CHRISTIAN (shouting):
  I am going to die!

CYRANO:
  Lower your voice!

CHRISTIAN (very softly):
  Die! . . .

CYRANO:
  The night is dark. . .

CHRISTIAN:
  Well?

CYRANO:
  It can be repaired.
  You do not deserve it. . . Stand there, wretch!
  There, in front of the balcony! I shall stand beneath it. . .
  And prompt thee with thy words.

CHRISTIAN:
  But. . .

CYRANO:
  Be quiet!

THE PAGES (reappearing at the back, to Cyrano):
  Hey!

CYRANO:
  Hush! . . .
  (He motions to them to speak softly.)

FIRST PAGE (in a half-voice):
  We have just serenaded
  Montfleury! . . .

CYRANO (softly, quickly):
  Go and lie in ambush,
  One at that street corner and the other at this one;
  And if some troublesome passerby comes this way,
  Play a tune!

SECOND PAGE:
  What sort of tune, Monsieur Gassendist?

CYRANO:
  A merry one for a woman, and for a man, a sad one!
  (The pages disappear, one at each street corner.—To Christian):
  Call her!

CHRISTIAN:
  Roxane!

CYRANO (picking up pebbles and throwing them at the windowpanes):
  Wait! A few pebbles.



Scene VII.

Roxane, Christian, Cyrano, at first hidden beneath the balcony.


ROXANE (partly opening her window):
  Who is calling me?

CHRISTIAN:
  I.

ROXANE:
  Who is “I”?

CHRISTIAN:
  Christian.

ROXANE (disdainfully):
  It is you?

CHRISTIAN:
  I should like to speak to you.

CYRANO (beneath the balcony, to Christian):
  Good. Good. Almost in a whisper.

ROXANE:
  No! You speak too poorly. Go away!

CHRISTIAN:
  Please! . . .

ROXANE:
  No! You no longer love me!

CHRISTIAN (as Cyrano prompts him with his words):
  To accuse me—righteous gods!—
  Of loving no longer. . . when. . . I love more!

ROXANE (who was about to close her window, stopping):
  Why, that is better!

CHRISTIAN (the same business):
  Love grows, cradled within my troubled soul. . .
  Which that cruel brat took for. . . a cradle!
